finding.claim: Unauthenticated SQL injection in /search: the raw `q` query parameter is interpolated into an f-string SQL LIKE clause, so any remote caller can read arbitrary data from the SQLite database (including sqlite_master and any other table) via UNION-based injection.
finding.source: app.py:11 request.args.get("q") — attacker-controlled GET parameter, no auth required
finding.sink: app.py:12 db.execute(f"SELECT id, name FROM products WHERE name LIKE '%{term}%'") — string concatenation into SQL; rows returned to the client at app.py:13 via jsonify

trace.note: /search route is registered with no auth decorator or before_request guard
term taken verbatim from request query string, no type, length, or character validation
term placed inside the single-quoted SQL literal via f-string; a value containing ' terminates the literal and the rest is parsed as SQL
result rows (attacker-chosen columns/tables via UNION) serialized and returned to the caller

finding.guards_checked: No authentication/authorization on the route (app.py:9-13). No input validation or escaping on term (app.py:11). Parameterized binding is used only in /product (app.py:18) and /by-owner (app.py:25), not here. Python sqlite3 rejects multi-statement execute, so the attack is limited to a single SELECT (read-only UNION/subquery exfiltration), not stacked writes. Repro: GET /search?q=x%25'%20UNION%20SELECT%20name,sql%20FROM%20sqlite_master--  (the first UNION column count matches the 2 selected columns, and `--` comments out the trailing %')

verdict.guard_found: none. app.py:9 is a bare @app.route("/search") with no auth decorator; app.py:11 takes q verbatim with no validation; app.py:12 interpolates it into the SQL via f-string with no parameter binding. A repo-wide grep found no before_request, login_required, after_request, or blueprint guards. Python's sqlite3 rejects multi-statement execute, so the impact is read-only UNION/subquery exfiltration, as the candidate states.
verdict.reason: The /search route at app.py:9 is anonymous, and the raw q value at app.py:11 is concatenated into the SQL at app.py:12 with no escaping or parameterization, so a UNION SELECT against sqlite_master (name, sql) is returned to the caller via jsonify at app.py:13; the candidate's repro payload has the right column count and comments out the trailing %'.</reason>
